title: An MRI decoder turns brain activity into text
summary: A noninvasive decoder reconstructs continuous text from fMRI that closely, and sometimes precisely, matches the original meaning in about half of trials (after dozens of hours of training with podcasts; it also works on silent videos). Published in Nature Neuroscience; it works only with cooperative participants and is not word-for-word transcription.

evidence.tested: A non-invasive fMRI decoder generated continuous text that conveyed the meaning of perceived speech, imagined speech and silent videos; the press release says it matched the original meaning in about half of trials and works only with cooperative participants.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not report participant numbers or semantic accuracy measures and states no explicit limitations; the press release says it is not word-for-word transcription.
evidence.ai_role: A decoder trained on fMRI recordings of cortical semantic representations generated word sequences matching the meaning of brain activity.
